I need to be direct about the risk this poses to the whole project. We need a more concrete solution.
I appreciate that, Aisyah. But 'when you can' sounds risky. With everything going on, we can't count on you having the time or energy. We need a more definite plan to get it finished.
I've stated my concern about the uncertainty of her plan and am waiting for a response.

Jun Jie has a point about the deadline being risky, but it feels a bit pushy right now. Aisyah's offered what she can. He's looking for someone else to pick up the work, I bet. I can't take it on. I'm already covering for someone else and I'm swamped. I'll just stay quiet and see what happens. This isn't my conversation to jump into yet.
Waiting to see how the conversation between Jun Jie and Aisyah develops.

I'll agree with Jun Jie.
He's right. 'Maybe' isn't going to work. We need to know how it's going to get done.
I've stated my position and am waiting to see how the others respond.

The best thing is to make it possible for someone else to finish it. I'll send them everything I have, but with very clear notes on what's missing. And I'll offer a specific time I can be available for questions. That's a concrete commitment, not just a vague promise. It shows I'm trying to solve the problem for the team, not just for myself.

You're right. Sorry. Okay, I'll send you everything I have right now, with detailed notes on what still needs to be done. The data is all there. If someone can take it over, I can make myself available for a call after 10 tonight if you have questions.
I've made a more concrete proposal. Now I wait for them to respond.

I've accepted Aisyah's plan and asked the team to decide how to reallocate the work. Waiting for their response.

Waiting for Shu Fen's answer.
